implementation_notes: Go's testing package provides the runner but no snapshot support; the idiomatic realization is the convention the standard library itself follows: reference files live under testdata/ (a directory the go tool ignores), a package-level var update = flag.Bool("update", false, ...) rewrites them when behaviour changes on purpose, and the test compares the captured output with os.ReadFile/bytes.Equal using subtests (t.Run) to name each case. That fifteen-line helper replaces the classic comparator, and it stays justified because it has no dependency and reads like every other Go test.
pitfalls: -update must stay opt-in and unset on CI: a build server that rewrites goldens destroys the net it is supposed to run.
A missing reference file must fail the test; a branch that writes when the file does not exist silently records whatever the buggy build produced.
Parallel subtests writing the same golden race; keep the update path serial and never call t.Parallel() on a case that writes.
Paths must resolve relative to the package directory (the working directory of `go test`), so moved test files need their testdata/ moved with them.

variants.name: gotest.tools/v3/golden package
variants.idiom_name: golden.Assert / golden.AssertBytes with the package's -update flag
variants.implementation_notes: The gotest.tools/v3/golden package wraps exactly the stdlib convention: golden.Assert compares a value against ./testdata/<name> and registers its own -test.update flag (golden.FlagUpdate) so references are rewritten only in a deliberate run. Choose it when several packages share the harness or when you want the comparison, the flag and the file layout maintained by a library instead of copied from package to package.
pitfalls: Assert accepts a value that must be converted to bytes by the supplied type, so a wrong golden.String/bytes choice silently compares the wrong representation.
The update flag is package-wide (-test.update), so a single run can rewrite every reference in the package at once; review the diff before committing.
